summary: Officers were sent to the 2500 block of Taft Highway for a man in a black shirt and pants reported to be lying on the sidewalk in front of a business and exposing himself.
Officers were sent to a phone store in the 10300 block of Main Street for a verbal disturbance with a customer, and a second caller reported the same thing.
Officers were sent to a mobile home park at 7:17 p.m. for a 15-year-old in a white shirt and black pants reported to be holding a gray handgun.

disposition: subject had left and was hiding
summary: Officers checked on a man in the 200 block of Hermosa Drive who said his roommates were forcing him to take medicine the hospital prescribed or leave the residence. He ran from the location and was hiding.
A semi was reported on fire at Inyo Street and East 19th Street. Engines, a truck and a battalion chief were sent, and the number 2 lane was blocked.
A crew was sent to the 500 block of R Street for a medical call, with units asked to approach from a distance.
Officers were sent to the 300 block of Bernard Street for two juveniles reported to be with a woman in her 40s who buys them alcohol.
A woman on a bicycle in a black hoodie and reddish leggings was reported to have got into an apartment through a window.
A driver flagged down an officer on northbound Interstate 5 north of Fort Tejon and said a man had tried to force him out of his vehicle and take his keys and wallet.
A vehicle was reported fully engulfed south of Hageman Road and Brundage Lane, blocking the northbound number 1 lane, with a crash reported at the same spot.
A fire alarm came in for a residence in the 1300 block of Sierra Summit Avenue.
A crew was sent to the 11400 block of Stockdale Highway for traumatic injuries.
A man in a white shirt and black pants who a caller said had grabbed at his waistband was reported in the 4500 block of Garnet Court, and the callers stayed on scene.

disposition: one driver asked for an ambulance; the other declined
summary: Two vehicles crashed just before 10 p.m. The driver who was rear-ended asked for an ambulance for pain, and the driver whose brakes failed and ran into him declined medical treatment.

disposition: driver extricated; hard closure of the lanes
summary: A semi rear-ended another semi on northbound Interstate 5 half a mile south of the Grapevine. One driver was pinned and firefighters freed him from the tractor-trailer, and crews asked for a hard closure of the lanes.
A crew was sent to the Navigation Center in the 1900 block of East Brundage Lane.
A company was sent to an outside fire just west of Road 28 and south of the county line.
A caller at a home improvement store reported vehicles doing donuts in the parking lot and blocking an employee's vehicle, and said one of them nearly hit an employee.
Officers were sent to the 1500 block of Country Club Drive for a man diagnosed as schizophrenic and bipolar who had stopped taking his medication.
A crew was sent to an apartment in the 3600 block of South Chester Avenue for an ill patient.
A man down near a shopping cart was reported at Mount Vernon Avenue and Height Street, and medical units staged nearby.
A crew was sent to the 400 block of Decatur Street for an unknown medical aid with a sheriff's unit pending.

area: Dr Martin Luther King Jr Boulevard
summary: Officers were sent to the 3300 block of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard after a woman in a black puffer jacket threw a baby bottle at a man.
A man in his 30s was reported lying in the roadway on Norris Road, not moving, with his breathing unknown, and medical units were cleared to respond.

A man got out of a white Ford F-150 stopped in the center divide on Interstate 5 and was reported to be punching the male driver. He may have crossed to the southbound side on foot, and a woman about 20 to 30 years old was with the truck.
Officers were sent to the 19400 block of Quinn Road to locate a subject.
A white box truck was reported at high speed on southbound Interstate 5, brake checking and flashing its high beams near Old River.
Officers were sent to the 1000 block of Altus Street for a disturbance.
A crew was sent to the 2400 block of Claire Street for difficulty breathing.
A crew was sent to a unit on E Street for a cardiac arrest.
A crew was sent to a home for a patient who had fainted.
An outside fire was reported on North Chester Avenue near a fast food restaurant that had burned before.
A full response went to a truck stop for a fire alarm with smoke reported from the restaurant area of the business. Crews found no fire, only a light haze, and confirmed that all occupants were out.
A crew was sent to the 3500 block of Big Al Avenue for difficulty breathing.
A residential fire alarm came in for the 24700 block of Sullivan Road, and the engine was canceled once the alarm was confirmed.
A crew was sent to an apartment complex for a psych problem and asked to stage until officers arrived.
A crew was sent to the 5400 block of Trailhead Street for difficulty breathing.

disposition: residents evacuated; entry team went in from the rear
summary: Officers worked an apartment complex through the early morning. Residents of several units were brought out through a garage door at the rear of the building, an armored vehicle was moved into position in front, and the entry team came in from the back. Officers found bullet holes in the doorway of an upstairs unit.
A small outside fire was reported, and one company was able to handle it.
A crew was sent to a mobile home park in the 400 block of East Roberts Lane for a stroke patient.
A crew was sent for a patient with difficulty breathing.
A crew was sent to an apartment in the 4300 block of White Lane for difficulty breathing.
A crew was sent to an apartment in the 600 block of Mable Avenue for an unknown medical aid and asked for a translator.
Two reports of shots heard came in at 4:33 a.m., six to eight rounds in the 10800 block of Royal Ascot Avenue and about 12 rounds in the 10000 block of Laurel Park Avenue.
A company was sent to an outside fire just north of the 14800 block of Woodward Avenue.
A crew was sent to an apartment at a senior living community in the 8200 block of Westwold Drive.

disposition: crews split up to search the tracks
summary: Crews were sent to look for a fire reported near the railroad tracks off Caliente-Bodfish Road and split up to search along the tracks.
Officers were sent to check on someone on foot near Sandrini Road and Highway 99 on the east side, wearing a red jacket and black pants.
A truck was sent to a commercial fire alarm in the 9100 block of Rosedale Highway.
A crew was sent to an apartment in the 1900 block of Palm Avenue.
Minor traffic collision near Workman Street in Bakersfield.
Traffic collision at Hageman Road and Verdugo Lane.
Vehicle and semi collision on Highway 99.
Possible crash involving white sedan near intersection.
Disorderly conduct reported on California Avenue.
Officer contact with resident at Verde Street unit.
Wildland fire reported near railroad by Horseshoe Bend.
Person in cardiac arrest near 45th Street West.
Hit-and-run crash with injury at 23rd and Chester.
